title: White Rice with Cheese and/or Cream Sauce, Fat Added

content.title: About
content.content: White rice prepared with a cheese or cream‑based sauce and added fat is a calorie‑dense side dish with a soft texture and a rich, buttery flavor. The fat increases the energy value and enhances the perception of taste.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cream sauces are often made from butter, cream, and cheese, giving the dish a luxurious mouthfeel.
In cooking, white rice is used as a neutral base that lets sauces shine.
Adding fat improves the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins such as A and D present in the sauce.
These dishes are traditional in both Asian and Mediterranean cuisines.
When cooked with the correct water‑to‑rice ratio, the grains stay separate and do not become mushy.

items.title: High Energy Content
items.content: The fat and cheese sauce raise the calorie count, which can be beneficial for individuals with increased energy needs.

items.title: Source of Calcium
items.content: Cheese sauce provides calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice supplies B1, B3 and B6 vitamins that support metabolism.

items.title: Fat‑Soluble Vitamins
items.content: The added fat aids the absorption of vitamins A, D, E and K if they are present in the sauce.

items.title: Enhanced Flavor Perception
items.content: Fat amplifies aroma and prolongs the taste experience.

items.title: High Calorie Density
items.content: The dish is calorie‑rich and may contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Saturated Fat Content
items.content: Cream sauces contain saturated fats, which in excess can raise cholesterol levels.

items.title: Lactose Intolerance
items.content: Cheese and cream may cause discomfort for people who are lactose intolerant.

items.title: Dairy Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to milk proteins.

items.title: Sodium Levels
items.content: Cheese sauces are often salty, which should be considered by those with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice hot, drizzled with the cheese or cream sauce. Garnish with fresh herbs, chopped parsley, or sautéed vegetables for variety. The dish pairs well with meat, fish, or vegetable patties.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Store the sauce separately and reheat together with the rice if needed. Frozen portions can be stored for up to 2 months.
